name: Gotham Green
lede: Gotham Green is a dark, slightly blue-leaning green named for Gotham, the old nickname for New York City.

sections.title: A city nickname's green
sections.body:
Wikipedia's entry on the word *Gotham* dates the nickname for New York City to Washington Irving's satirical writing in 1807, well before it named a fictional Batman city [3]. Our library traces this color name only to a Wikipedia list, with no date given for when the color itself was coined [1]. Measured in LCH, it sits at lightness 32, a dark green with a hue angle leaning toward blue rather than yellow [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[billiard]], 3.0 units of CIEDE2000 away and described as duller [1]. [[pearl-opal-green]] sits a little farther out at 3.6, reading bluer, and [[verdure]] at 4.1, reading greener [1]. Against those three, Gotham Green is the darkest of the group [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 29 of 23,781 paintings (0.12 percent), rarer than 63 percent of the named colors, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 8 of 1,674 paintings, at 4.6 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, 76 percent of the time, a role measured by lightness rank within the canvas rather than by the raw hex match [2]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
